card.name: Start of author names in citations
card.fires_on: The first piece of a scholar's or author's name in reference lists and in-text citations, often right after a dash, semicolon or 'and'. The name is usually split across pieces, such as G|ellman or Br|igitte.

modes.label: Reference list entries
modes.description: First piece of an author's surname after a dash or in a bibliography line.
modes.example: in New York. New Press, 2005. ISBN 1-56584-997-3. -<< G>>ellman, David N. Emanc

modes.label: In-text citations
modes.description: The start of the next author's name after a semicolon in a parenthetical citation.
modes.example: Elis and Boiotia (e.g., Thebes), it was approved of and even celebrated (cf. Dover, 1989;<< Hal>>perin, 1990

modes.label: Names in a list of people
modes.description: A first or given name piece within a list of academics or speakers.
modes.example: Dutch Sephardic Jewry in the Age of Rembrandt and Spinoza. The speakers were: Joh<<athan>> Israel, the Amado Visiting Professor

card.writes: It pushes toward words from the social sciences and scholarship, such as ethnography, anthropology and interviewed.
card.plain: It marks the start of an academic author's name in a citation, where social-science text tends to follow.
